answer: Auditors decode the graft cipher tree by tree on each row. Registration leases one orchard row of 20 rooted trees, locking 180 units for 12 epochs; the cipher records each tree's graft sequence, so one row supports one identity: rooted stock cannot be lent or moved without killing it. Auditors scan leaf spectra through a prism at random visits; a spectrum or cipher mismatch, or one sequence claimed twice, is public proof that slashes the 180. An honest agent tends one row; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 rows, 20,000 trees and 180,000 locked at once. The 180 is refunded only after 12 clean epochs.
